newsitem.title: USA: Judge throws out kidnapping charge in Kelly trial. [CORRECTED 20:49 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Judge throws out kidnapping charge in Kelly trial. [CORRECTED 20:49 GMT]

text.p: A Connecticut judge on Thursday threw out a kidnapping charge in the rape retrial of former high school wrestling star Alex Kelly.

Kelly's girlfriend, Amy Molitor, disclosed on the witness stand on Thursday that she was engaged to be married to Kelly, who is accused of raping a 16-year-old neighbour in Darien, Connecticut in February 1986. (Corrects year)
The alleged rape took place after a party in a vehicle loaned to Kelly by Molitor's family. Kelly's defence is that the sex was consensual.
Kelly, 30, fled the United States and lived as a fugitive for eight years before surrendering in Switzerland in 1995.

He now faces a single count of first-degree sexual assault, which carries a sentence on conviction of up to 20 years in jail. The kidnapping charge could have brought a 10- to 25-year term, although both sentences might have run concurrently.

Stamford Superior Court Judge Kevin Tierney said there was no evidence Kelly abducted the teenager, who is now a 27-year-old sales representative at a pharmaceutical company. He agreed with Kelly's lawyer, Thomas Puccio, that Connecticut's kidnapping law was "vague" and not well-written.

Molitor, who was Kelly's girlfriend at the time of the alleged rape, took the witness stand when the defence opened its case on Thursday. Asked by Puccio about her relationship with Kelly, she said they became engaged on April 4 of this year but did not indicate if a wedding date has been set.
Molitor, a 27-year-old bartender in Darien, told the court she first met Kelly at an ice cream parlour in 1983. She said she now lives with Kelly's parents in Darien.

Kelly's first trial ended in a hung jury last November. He fled the United States on the eve of his original scheduled trial in 1987, embarking on an eight-year odyssey through 15 countries that included time on the ski slopes of Europe.
Authorities have said his travels were financed by his wealthy parents.
Kelly was also accused in February 1986 of raping a 17-year-old girl in a separate incident. The two alleged rapes are being tried separately. No date has been set for the second trial.
